failedBootstrap.explanation: The first attempt used legacy getWorkspace({types:true}), which built one synthetic root-options Project and manually added broad globs, and launched it with bare node. Bare node exposed a 4192 MiB heap and OOMed near that ceiling. It bypassed pnpm-workspace.yaml NODE_OPTIONS; pnpm exec node exposes a 16480 MiB heap. The successful audit uses sequential native-config Projects and exits between configs.

refusedArtifacts.reason: invalid zero-file artifact from unnormalized /repo/. prefix; excluded

boundedRemainder: Root-owned top-level config TypeScript files were not traversed after the all-root retry was terminated because it duplicated already-covered corpora. The nine packages, tooling, Node tests, DOM tests, ISO tests, scripts, and Playwright are complete.

trpcBridge.limitation: The general scanner's import-name origin filter did not resolve inferInput/inferOutput through TypeReference import aliases; these projection counts are structural ast-grep corroboration, not checker counts. confirmedFindings.title: 307 TypeID request/import schemas validate only non-empty strings while claiming prefix-validated brands
confirmedFindings.population: 307 of 338 production brandedId<T>() calls resolve T to a TypeIdOf alias; 31 resolve to permitted prefixless brands.
confirmedFindings.scenario: A caller sends `chat_not-a-typeid`, or a well-shaped `persona_...` in a ChatId field. brandedId accepts it and hands domain code a ChatId. Most owner-scoped reads later collapse this to NOT_FOUND, but the trust-boundary type claim is false; imported AssetId fields likewise carry opaque foreign strings as Orb AssetId before owner resolution.
confirmedFindings.repair: Split the gate's accepted helpers by checker-resolved target alias: require typeIdSchema(ID_PREFIX.x) for TypeIdOf and brandedId only for prefixless Branded aliases. Migrate by bounded domain batches with malformed and wrong-prefix negative tests; keep foreign portable ids as strings until owner-scoped resolution returns an actual AssetId.

confirmedFindings.title: Seven inference model/provider columns remain unbranded, and the ST importer can write arbitrary strings
confirmedFindings.scenario: An imported ST file supplies arbitrary model/provider text. chat-input forwards it and import-write persists it, so the stored identity has no registry-validation provenance. Adding only Drizzle $type<ModelId/ProviderId> would then make the compiler trust those same unvalidated bytes and defend a lie.
confirmedFindings.repair: Treat this as one producer-to-storage change: brand all seven columns, validate producer values against provider/model registries, map invalid imported provider/model values to the ruled unknown representation, and add one negative producer test per column. model_stats.provider needs ProviderId | '(unknown)'.

confirmedFindings.title: Caller-authored workload dependencies cross the owner boundary without validation
confirmedFindings.scenario: User A starts a singular workload with dependsOn containing a known User-B workload id. The row is persisted under A, but the scheduler resolves dependency ids without owner scope. A's job then waits, runs, or fails based on B's live status, exposing existence/status. A malformed or absent nonempty id also permanently poisons A's row into dependency_failed.
confirmedFindings.repair: At the start verb, validate every dependency's TypeID shape, existence, and allowed ownership/authority before insert; preserve the unscoped engine read only for server-authorized cross-owner edges. Add cross-owner, absent, and malformed dependency tests.

confirmedFindings.title: Inference streaming callbacks manufacture an empty ChatId when chatId is optional
confirmedFindings.scenario: A valid backend request supplies onDelta but omits chatId. OpenAI-compatible, Anthropic, and agent-sdk paths emit ChatDeltaEvent with chatId='' typed as ChatId. Consumers cannot distinguish missing identity from a real chat identity at the type level.
confirmedFindings.repair: Make the callback arm require chatId as a discriminated request contract, or suppress delta emission when chatId is absent. Remove all three empty casts and test onDelta+missing-chatId.

confirmedFindings.title: Disabled client queries and an invite fallback use empty strings typed as entity brands
confirmedFindings.scenario: Query-option builders receive '' typed as ChatId/PresetId/MessageId while enabled=false or as an inert row; a future enable/order change can send the fake identity. Invite preview can return hostHandle='' typed Handle if the asserted host invariant fails.
confirmedFindings.repair: Use skipToken/conditional option construction or nullable inert types instead of branded sentinels. Make missing host an invariant/domain error rather than minting an empty Handle.

confirmedFindings.title: BroadcastChannel parsing returns any string as Handle
confirmedFindings.scenario: A same-origin stale tab or extension posts {kind:'session-recovered',handle:'not a valid handle'}. asSessionMessage returns it as Handle. Current consumers only compare/reload, so no privilege escalation was confirmed, but the parser's stronger return type is false.
confirmedFindings.repair: Use the canonical Handle parser at the channel boundary, or keep handle as string until the server-authenticated identity read validates it.

coverageGapsAndPlannedWork.title: AppRouter output types cross JSON without runtime output schemas
coverageGapsAndPlannedWork.fact: The server has 423 terminal procedures (252 mutations, 169 queries, 2 subscriptions), 367 input validators, and zero .output() validators. Client code derives 193 inferOutput and 179 inferInput generic projections structurally from the singular AppRouter bridge.
coverageGapsAndPlannedWork.consequence: This is an honesty/coverage gap, not a confirmed exploit by itself: server construction is trusted and JSON serialization can still drift from inferred output shapes.
coverageGapsAndPlannedWork.plan: Inventory high-consequence outputs first (brands, credential-adjacent data, discriminated events, Date/Map/Set/BigInt-like values), add selective runtime output schemas where the transport value matters, and build a checker-based bridge lens instead of banning the intended type-only edge.

coverageGapsAndPlannedWork.title: Complete producer/read graph for 264 brand-bearing Drizzle $type sites remains unbuilt
coverageGapsAndPlannedWork.fact: The checker closed the $type denominator: 350 total, 254 direct-brand, 10 additional brand-bearing containers, 86 unbranded. The known seven inference model/provider omissions were traced end-to-end; every producer/read/downstream sink for all 264 brand-bearing sites was not manually adjudicated.
coverageGapsAndPlannedWork.plan: Build a table-symbol-based writer/reader graph that resolves Drizzle insert/update/select symbols and follows values into registry/routing/AAD/tenant/key consumers. Refuse unresolved table/column origins rather than widening by name.

coverageGapsAndPlannedWork.title: Zod semantic denominator is closed; business-intent adjudication remains
coverageGapsAndPlannedWork.fact: 569 production transform/preprocess/coerce/catch/default/pipe/prefault operator sites were checker-classified; 347 have mutually non-equivalent input/output types and 13 produce brand-bearing output.
coverageGapsAndPlannedWork.plan: Review the 13 brand-producing output sites and schemas feeding untrusted ingress first. Keep defaults/catches that construct their declared output; file only sites whose runtime construction does not justify the stronger type.

limitations: The report is package-complete and separately covers tooling, Node tests, DOM tests, ISO tests, scripts, and Playwright. Root-only top-level TypeScript config files are the explicit bounded remainder.

safeParse success/data tracking is intraprocedural and symbol-based within the containing function; escapes through returned closures, object aliasing, or higher-order callbacks are not a full interprocedural proof.
Checker populations establish type relationships and symbol origins. They do not prove business authorization; confirmed defects were manually traced through load-bearing producers/consumers.
The 569-site Zod operator population is mechanically closed, but all 347 input/output-different sites were not individually judged for business intent in this tranche.
No runtime mutation or repository edit was performed; this is a read-only audit.
